author: PicoMarkdownView contributors
description: Practical showcase examples authored for this app; separate from the pinned upstream Prism grammar cases.

examples.title: Swift: decode and transform structured data
examples.description: Decode a small payload, filter its values, and format the results. The same document can contain code, explanatory prose, and selectable output.

examples.title: Python: summarize a data pipeline
examples.description: Group readings by station, discard missing values, and calculate a rounded average with the standard library.

examples.title: TypeScript: reusable generic grouping
examples.description: Keep the item type and key type while grouping structured records into a map.

examples.title: Rust: handle valid and invalid input
examples.description: A Result carries either the converted temperature or the original parse error; a match handles both outcomes.

examples.title: JSON: a nested configuration
examples.description: Strings, numbers, arrays, booleans, and null values share one highlighted block.

examples.title: SQL: aggregate the same readings
examples.description: Create a small in-memory dataset, then group and filter it with a common table expression.

examples.title: Shell: write and summarize a local file
examples.description: A temporary file keeps this example self-contained. Quoted variables and a cleanup trap make the flow easy to follow.
examples.source:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$workspace"' EXIT
cat > "$workspace/readings.csv" <<'CSV'
station,celsius
Harbor,18.4
Hilltop,21.0
Forest,16.8
CSV

awk -F, 'NR > 1 { printf "%-8s %4.1f °C\n", $1, $2 }' "$workspace/readings.csv"
